subject: SLO instrumentation and temporary sampling carveout - procurement packet
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightwave.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: BrightWave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO instrumentation and measurement questions for procurement packet

Jonas,

Thanks for sending the initial order form. Procurement had a few follow-ups specific to how SLOs are measured, alerts are generated, and what access BrightWave will have to live metrics. We've collated them below so they can be added to our vendor packet. Please respond with concise answers we can include in the procurement submission.

1) Availability definition: How does Redwood define "availability" for model inference? Is it control-plane, inference endpoint response, or both? What is the exact numerator/denominator and measurement window?
2) Latency SLAs: Which latency percentiles are contractual (p50/p95/p99)? Are streaming responses included in latency measurements?
3) Measurement cadence & sampling: Do you compute SLOs on full-sample data or a sampled stream? If sampling, what sampling ratio and how does that affect small-traffic customers?
4) Alerting & incident visibility: What thresholds trigger customer-facing alerts? Can BrightWave subscribe to webhooks or SNMP/PagerDuty notifications for incidents affecting our region?
5) Dashboard & raw data access: Will BrightWave get read-only access to dashboards (Grafana) and the ability to export raw metric data (CSV/Prometheus)? What are retention windows for raw and aggregated metrics?
6) Credits & remediation: How are SLA credits calculated and awarded? What is the claims process and typical turnaround?
7) Exceptions & carveouts: We expect an instrumentation ramp for the first 30 days post-commencement. Can Redwood include a temporary carveout to allow sampling-based measurements during onboarding? If so, how is that documented in the agreement?

If you can return a short packet by Tuesday (22 Jul) that we can attach to the procurement record, that would be ideal. Also attaching our template questionnaire for reference (attached to this email).

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Procurement
BrightWave

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightwave.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, BrightWave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO instrumentation and measurement questions for procurement packet

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers you can drop into your procurement packet. I've attached a short PDF with examples and a spreadsheet that shows the credits calculation we typically use. If anything needs to be expanded, flag it and we can add a one-pager.

1) Availability definition:
- What we measure: availability = successful inference responses / total inference requests to the provisioned endpoint (HTTP 200-like success).
- Scope: measurement is at the inference egress (application layer) for the model endpoint(s) serving your traffic. We do not count control-plane scheduling delays in the availability numerator/denominator for the public SLA; those are surfaced separately in operational reports.
- Window: Availability is computed on a rolling 30-day window for SLA purposes, with daily aggregation and a 1-minute collection cadence.

2) Latency SLAs:
- Contracted percentiles: p50 and p95 are provided for informational purposes; p99 is the contractual threshold for latency-based credits.
- Streaming: Streaming responses are excluded from p99 inference latency SLA calculations by default because they have different response semantics. We measure streaming latency separately (initial response time + per-chunk lag) and can include those metrics in the dashboard.

3) Measurement cadence & sampling:
- By default we use full-sample measurement for high-volume tenants. For new tenants or low-traffic workloads, we may use a lightweight sampling agent during the instrumentation window (see #7). Typical production sampling ratio for low-volume onboarding is 5% of requests (uniform random sampling), which preserves percentile estimates while minimizing ingestion cost.
- Impact on small customers: If sampling is used, we apply conservative bias-correction and report confidence intervals on percentile estimates. We also provide a sampling metadata field so customers understand the effective sample size.

4) Alerting & incident visibility:
- Thresholds: Customer-facing alerts are configurable but default to availability drop of >0.5 percentage points over a 15-minute window or p95 latency degradation >2x baseline for three consecutive 5-minute buckets.
- Integrations: We provide PagerDuty, webhook, and email notification integrations. For enterprise customers, we can provision a dedicated incident channel and send raw metric snapshots during incidents.

5) Dashboard & raw data access:
- Access: BrightWave will receive a read-only Grafana workspace invite and a tokened Prometheus read-only API key for metric exports.
- Retention: Raw metrics retention is 30 days; rolled-up aggregates (per-minute summaries) are retained 12 months. Exports to CSV are available on-demand for the last 30 days; we can provide scheduled export jobs for longer retention on request (add-on).

6) Credits & remediation:
- Calculation: Credits are calculated against the monthly invoice as a percentage based on the degree of SLO miss. The spreadsheet attached ("slo_credits_calculation.xlsx") shows the tiered formula (e.g., availability 99.9–99.5 => 5% credit, <99.5 => 15%).
- Claims: Customers must open a ticket within 30 days of the incident window. We validate against metric stores (immutable measurement keys) and issue credits on the following billing cycle (standard).

7) Exceptions & carveouts (instrumentation ramp):
- Proposal: We agree to a temporary carveout for the first 30 days following live traffic start that allows sampling-based measurement (up to 5% sampling) while instrumentation is finalized. During that period, SLO calculations will include a note that measurements are sampled and credits are applied only after a minimum sample-size threshold is met.
- Contract language: We can add a short clause: "Instrumentation Ramp: For the first 30 calendar days following the Service Commencement Date, Redwood may apply sampling for telemetry collection. SLO credits during this period will be issued only if the sample size meets the documented confidence threshold. Full SLO enforcement resumes thereafter."

Next steps:
- Attached packet includes the short PDF (redwood_slo_response_packet.pdf) and an onboarding invite for the Grafana workspace (dashboard_onboarding_invite.txt). If agreed, we can insert the proposed clause into the MSA and provide a one-line summary for the procurement sheet.

I'll be available Wednesday/Thursday for a 30-minute call to walk through the credits spreadsheet if you want to run sample scenarios.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Jonas — thanks for the thorough answers and the attachments. A couple quick clarifications before I slot this into the procurement packet:

- For the sampling carveout, can you confirm the minimum sample-size threshold used to qualify SLO crediting? Procurement needs a deterministic rule (e.g., at least N requests or 1000 requests per 30-day window).
- For the credit tiers, can you provide a worked example for July (assume 99.6% measured availability, 3 incidents during the calendar month) so our finance team can model potential credits?
- Lastly, we require an explicit SLA clause that includes the timeframe for issuing credits (e.g., within 45 days of validated claim). Can you confirm Redwood's standard timing?

If you can send those 3 items today we can close procurement on Friday.

Best,
Elena

Subject: Re: SLO instrumentation and measurement questions for procurement packet

Elena —

Quick answers inline and I've attached a short worked example in the credits spreadsheet tab "BrightWave Example".

- Minimum sample-size threshold: We use a deterministic rule of 1,000 sampled requests per 30-day window for sampled measurements to be eligible for credit. If the sample is below this threshold, credits are deferred until the full-sample period or the instrumentation ramp ends. We will include the exact language in the MSA clause.

- Worked example (July): Assume BrightWave had 1,000,000 total requests in July, measured availability 99.6% (so 4,000 failed requests). Under our tiered credit table: 99.9–99.5 => 5% credit. Because measured availability is 99.6, BrightWave would receive a 5% credit on the monthly service fee for July. The workbook tab shows how multiple incidents within the month map to the same aggregated availability delta and the resulting credit.

- Credit timing: Standard turnaround is validation within 30 days of claim and credit applied on the next billing cycle (up to 45 days in edge cases). We'll state: "Validated claims will be credited within one billing cycle following verification (typically 30–45 days)."

I'll drop the small wording updates into the MSA draft and send a short addendum for signature. If you'd like the 30-minute walkthrough, I can calendar that today at 4pm PT.

Cheers,
Jonas
